faqs.question: What does the T-ALL MRD Test measure?
faqs.answer: The T-ALL MRD Test analyze and quantify residual leukemic cells in the bone marrow or peripheral blood in patients with T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (T-ALL).

faqs.question: Why is the T-ALL MRD Test done?
faqs.answer: • To monitor treatment effectiveness in patients with T-ALL • To detect MRD after treatment • To assess the risk of disease recurrence

faqs.question: When is the T-ALL MRD Test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: The T-ALL MRD Test is recommended for patients with T-ALL.

faqs.question: What if the results of the T-ALL MRD Test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: If the T-ALL MRD Test results are abnormal, it may indicate residual cancer cells or a higher risk of disease recurrence.

faqs.question: What to expect during the T-ALL MRD Test?
faqs.answer: During the test, a sample of bone marrow is collected using a needle. The sample is sent to the laboratory for analysis using flow cytometry.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the T-ALL MRD Test?
faqs.answer: • Inform your doctor about any medications or supplements you are taking. Also, tell them if you have any specific requirements. • Provide your medical history and any relevant hemato-pathological reports to your doctor • Follow any additional instructions given by your doctor.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the T-ALL MRD Test?
faqs.answer: • Hemato-pathological reports: To provide a comprehensive understanding of the disease and monitor treatment response • Genetic testing: To identify specific genetic abnormalities associated with T-ALL

faqs.question: What is the T-ALL MRD Test also known as?
faqs.answer: Minimal residual disease test for T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (T-ALL)

faqs.question: What is T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia?
faqs.answer: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (T-ALL) is a type of blood cancer that affects immature T-cells. It is characterised by an overproduction of abnormal T-cells in the bone marrow.
